Importance-sampling diagnostics of a vector of log importance ratios

Source: R/calc_is_diagnostics.R
calc_is_diagnostics.Rd

Reports the effective sample size and the Pareto \(\hat k\) of the importance weights \(r_i \propto \exp(x_i)\), \(x\) = log_lik. MOSAIC draws parameters from the prior and scores them with the log-likelihood \(\ell\), so the weights a posterior gives the draws follow from the scored values; what the numbers describe depends on what is passed in.

Usage

calc_is_diagnostics(log_lik, method = c("kish", "perplexity"))

Arguments

log_lik

Numeric vector of log-likelihoods, one per draw. Non-finite entries are dropped.

method

Character; ESS estimator passed to calc_model_ess. One of "kish" (default) or "perplexity".

Value

A named list with n, ess_is, ess_is_prop, khat, khat_status and n_positive_ratios.

Details

Tempered input, eta * log_lik

The weights of the coarsened posterior \(w_i \propto \exp(\eta \ell_i)\), \(\eta = \alpha / n_{obs}\), that MOSAIC actually builds. Its \(\hat k\) is the validity guard of calc_convergence_status (.mosaic_khat_tempered()): below 0.5 the ESS and its projection can be trusted; 0.5-0.7 usable but the Monte Carlo error converges slowly; at or above 0.7 the importance-sampling estimates are unreliable (Vehtari et al. 2024).

Untempered input, log_lik (\(\eta = 1\))

The likelihood-concentration numbers. With thousands of scored cells and a stochastic likelihood the untempered ratios span thousands of log units, so ess_is is about 1 and \(\hat k\) is huge or undefined whatever the fit. They measure how sharply the raw likelihood ranks the draws; they do not say whether the sampler explored the posterior, no posterior is built from them, and MOSAIC reports them in JSON only.

ess_is

The Kish (or perplexity) ESS of the normalised ratios, without any truncation.

khat

The Pareto \(\hat k\) shape statistic of PSIS (Vehtari et al. 2024), estimated with the empirical-Bayes profile likelihood of Zhang & Stephens (2009). NA with an explanatory khat_status when the tail cannot be fitted: fewer than 20 draws, tied tail ratios (nearly flat weights), or ratios that underflow to zero.

References

Vehtari A, Simpson D, Gelman A, Yao Y, Gabry J (2024). Pareto smoothed importance sampling. JMLR 25(72):1-58.

Zhang J, Stephens MA (2009). A new and efficient estimation method for the generalized Pareto distribution. Technometrics 51(3):316-325.

Examples

# Well-behaved importance weights: ESS a healthy fraction of n, small khat
set.seed(1)
calc_is_diagnostics(rnorm(1000, sd = 0.5))
#> $n
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $ess_is
#> [1] 765.7633
#> 
#> $ess_is_prop
#> [1] 0.7657633
#> 
#> $khat
#> [1] 0.1238871
#> 
#> $khat_status
#> [1] "good: finite IS variance"
#> 
#> $n_positive_ratios
#> [1] 1000
#> 

# Coarsened posterior of scored draws: pass the tempered log-likelihood
ll <- -2000 * (runif(5000) - 0.4)^2
calc_is_diagnostics((10 / 1000) * ll)$khat
#> [1] -1.752454
